items.prompt: A function is intended to return the maximum element of an array. Which input shape requires an explicit contract decision before implementation?

options.text: An array whose values are all equal.

feedback.reason: A maximum is undefined for an empty input unless the contract specifies a sentinel, error, or optional result.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “An empty array.”. A singleton has an unambiguous maximum: its only value. Increasing and all-equal shapes are also well-defined. Empty input changes the existence of the result itself.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: A maximum is undefined for an empty input unless the contract specifies a sentinel, error, or optional result.

items: A one-element array. — Its only element exists and is therefore the maximum; no extra return convention is needed.
A strictly increasing array. — The maximum exists and is the final value.
An array whose values are all equal. — Every value is a valid maximum, so the returned value is still unambiguous.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.single_element: Its only element exists and is therefore the maximum; no extra return convention is needed.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.strictly_increasing: The maximum exists and is the final value.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.all_equal: Every value is a valid maximum, so the returned value is still unambiguous.

items.prompt: A function checks whether an array is non-decreasing by comparing adjacent elements. What should it return for an empty array and a one-element array under the usual universal-condition contract?

options.text: false for empty, true for one element.
true for empty, false for one element.

feedback.reason: Neither shape contains an adjacent inversion that violates non-decreasing order.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “true for both inputs.”. The property says every adjacent pair must satisfy left <= right. Empty and singleton arrays contain no adjacent pairs, so no counterexample exists.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: Neither shape contains an adjacent inversion that violates non-decreasing order.

items: false for both inputs. — The absence of pairs does not create a violating pair.
false for empty, true for one element. — The same no-counterexample reasoning applies to both shapes.
true for empty, false for one element. — A one-element array also has no adjacent inversion.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.both_false: The absence of pairs does not create a violating pair.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.empty_false_single_true: The same no-counterexample reasoning applies to both shapes.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.empty_true_single_false: A one-element array also has no adjacent inversion.

items.prompt: A scan looks for a pair of adjacent equal values. Which input lengths can never contain such a pair?

options.text: Every input length can contain an adjacent equal pair.

feedback.reason: An adjacent pair requires at least two positions.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “Length 0 or 1.”. Length 0 has no values and length 1 has no neighbor. Length 2 can contain a pair, for example [5, 5].

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: An adjacent pair requires at least two positions.

items: Length 1 or 2. — A two-element input can contain exactly one adjacent pair.
Only length 0. — A singleton also lacks the second position required to form an adjacent pair.
Every input length can contain an adjacent equal pair. — Inputs shorter than two elements cannot contain any pair.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_or_two: A two-element input can contain exactly one adjacent pair.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.only_zero: A singleton also lacks the second position required to form an adjacent pair.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.all_lengths: Inputs shorter than two elements cannot contain any pair.

items.prompt: A stable deduplication function keeps the first occurrence of every value. Which shape produces the smallest possible logical output for a non-empty input of length n?

options.text: The sequence alternates between two distinct values.

feedback.reason: When all values are equal, stable deduplication retains exactly one occurrence.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “All n values are equal.”. All-distinct and strictly increasing inputs retain n values. Alternating two values retain two distinct values. The all-equal shape minimizes output length at one.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: When all values are equal, stable deduplication retains exactly one occurrence.

items: All n values are distinct. — No value can be removed because every occurrence is unique.
Values are strictly increasing. — Strict increase makes all n values distinct, so deduplication retains all n positions.
The sequence alternates between two distinct values. — Stable deduplication retains the first occurrence of each value, leaving two values rather than the minimum of one.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.all_distinct: No value can be removed because every occurrence is unique.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.strictly_increasing: Strict increase makes all n values distinct, so deduplication retains all n positions.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.alternating_two_values: Stable deduplication retains the first occurrence of each value, leaving two values rather than the minimum of one.

items.prompt: A filter keeps values greater than zero. What logical output length should be expected when every input value fails the predicate?

feedback.reason: A filter may legally produce an empty result even when the input is non-empty.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “0”. The output contains exactly the occurrences satisfying the predicate. If none do, the valid result has length zero.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: A filter may legally produce an empty result even when the input is non-empty.

items: 1 — Filtering does not retain a fallback element unless the contract explicitly requires one.
n — Retaining all n values would contradict the fact that every value fails.
The output length is undefined. — An empty filtered sequence is a well-defined result.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one: Filtering does not retain a fallback element unless the contract explicitly requires one.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.n: Retaining all n values would contradict the fact that every value fails.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.undefined: An empty filtered sequence is a well-defined result.

items.prompt: A filter keeps values greater than zero from a non-empty input of length n. Which input shape produces a logical output length equal to n?

options.text: No input value satisfies the predicate.
Every input value satisfies the predicate.
Only the first value satisfies the predicate.
Exactly every second value satisfies the predicate.

feedback.reason: The output retains one occurrence for every passing input occurrence.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “Every input value satisfies the predicate.”. When all values pass, no position is removed and the logical result length remains n.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: The output retains one occurrence for every passing input occurrence.

items: No input value satisfies the predicate. — Every occurrence is rejected, so the logical result length is 0 rather than n.
Only the first value satisfies the predicate. — Exactly one occurrence is retained; for a general non-empty length n, that does not guarantee length n.
Exactly every second value satisfies the predicate. — This retains only a subset of the n positions.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.none_pass: Every occurrence is rejected, so the logical result length is 0 rather than n.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.only_first_passes: Exactly one occurrence is retained; for a general non-empty length n, that does not guarantee length n.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.alternating: This retains only a subset of the n positions.

items.prompt: Which of these shapes should be included when testing a stable deduplication function? Select all that apply.

options.text: Only one already sorted, duplicate-free input.
Duplicate values are separated by other values.

feedback.reason: The test set should exercise no removals, maximal removals, and non-adjacent repetitions.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “All values are distinct.”, “All values are equal.”, “Duplicate values are separated by other values.”. These shapes expose accidental deletion, incorrect output length, and algorithms that detect only adjacent duplicates.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: The test set should exercise no removals, maximal removals, and non-adjacent repetitions.

items: Only one already sorted, duplicate-free input. — One easy shape cannot reveal behavior under repeated or separated values.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.only_sorted_unique: One easy shape cannot reveal behavior under repeated or separated values.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.all_distinct: It verifies that unique values are not removed.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.all_equal: It verifies maximal duplicate collapse and the minimum non-empty output size.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.separated_duplicates: It catches implementations that confuse adjacent-run compression with global deduplication.

items.prompt: A normalizer removes every punctuation character. What should it return when the input consists entirely of punctuation?

options.text: One punctuation character as a placeholder.
No result, because normalization requires at least one retained character.

feedback.reason: A valid normalization may produce an empty canonical representation.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “An empty normalized sequence.”. Every input occurrence belongs to the ignored category, so none is retained. The empty sequence remains a concrete, comparable result.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: A valid normalization may produce an empty canonical representation.

items: One punctuation character as a placeholder. — Adding a placeholder introduces data not present in the contract.
The unchanged input sequence. — This fails to remove characters explicitly declared ignorable.
No result, because normalization requires at least one retained character. — An empty canonical result is well-defined unless the contract says otherwise.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_punctuation: Adding a placeholder introduces data not present in the contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.unchanged_input: This fails to remove characters explicitly declared ignorable.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.undefined: An empty canonical result is well-defined unless the contract says otherwise.

items.prompt: A sequence is already in canonical normalized form. Which behavior is expected from an idempotent normalizer?

options.text: The final element is removed to mark completion.
The sequence is always sorted, even when sorting is not part of the contract.

feedback.reason: An idempotent normalizer maps canonical input to itself.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “It remains unchanged.”. Repeated normalization should not keep changing a representation that already satisfies every canonical rule.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: An idempotent normalizer maps canonical input to itself.

items: The final element is removed to mark completion. — Normalization must not delete meaningful data merely to signal execution.
The sequence is always sorted, even when sorting is not part of the contract. — Sorting is legal only if order is declared irrelevant.
Every retained value is duplicated. — Adding occurrences changes an already canonical representation, violating both preservation and idempotence.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.remove_last: Normalization must not delete meaningful data merely to signal execution.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_again: Sorting is legal only if order is declared irrelevant.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.duplicate_values: Adding occurrences changes an already canonical representation, violating both preservation and idempotence.

items.prompt: A function compares two sequences position by position. Which shape difference can allow an immediate false result before examining corresponding values?

options.text: The sequences have the same length.
The sequences have different lengths and equality requires every position to match.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “The sequences have different lengths and equality requires every position to match.”. If lengths differ, one sequence contains an unmatched position regardless of the values in the shared prefix. Equal length is necessary but not sufficient.

items: Both sequences are empty. — Their lengths match and neither has an unmatched position, so shape alone cannot justify false.
Both sequences contain one value. — Their values still need comparison; the shape alone does not prove inequality.
The sequences have the same length. — Equal length permits equality but does not determine it.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.both_empty: Their lengths match and neither has an unmatched position, so shape alone cannot justify false.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.both_singleton: Their values still need comparison; the shape alone does not prove inequality.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.same_length: Equal length permits equality but does not determine it.

items.prompt: A function groups consecutive equal values into runs. How many runs are produced by [2, 2, 1, 2, 2]?

feedback.reason: Run boundaries depend on adjacency, so separated occurrences of the same value form different runs.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “3”. The runs are [2, 2], [1], and [2, 2]. Global value identity does not merge non-adjacent runs.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: Run boundaries depend on adjacency, so separated occurrences of the same value form different runs.

items: 2 — This incorrectly merges the two separated runs of value 2.
1 — The value changes twice, creating additional run boundaries.
5 — Equal adjacent values belong to the same run rather than separate runs.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.two_runs: This incorrectly merges the two separated runs of value 2.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_run: The value changes twice, creating additional run boundaries.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.five_runs: Equal adjacent values belong to the same run rather than separate runs.

items.prompt: Which shapes expose the minimum-length boundary for a three-element window? Select all that apply.

options.text: Length 2, where no legal window exists.
Length 3, where exactly one legal window exists.
Length 4, where two legal starts exist.

feedback.reason: The largest illegal shape, smallest legal shape, and next legal shape reveal the boundary transition.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “Length 2, where no legal window exists.”, “Length 3, where exactly one legal window exists.”, “Length 4, where two legal starts exist.”. Lengths 2, 3, and 4 verify zero, one, and multiple window placements. A single large input does not isolate the threshold.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: The largest illegal shape, smallest legal shape, and next legal shape reveal the boundary transition.

items: Only one large random input. — A large case may pass despite an off-by-one error at the minimum legal length.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.only_large_random: A large case may pass despite an off-by-one error at the minimum legal length.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.length_two: It verifies that the algorithm rejects a sequence one element too short.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.length_three: It verifies acceptance of exactly one minimum-size window.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.length_four: It verifies continuation beyond the first legal placement.

items.prompt: Which of these shapes are useful for testing a frequency-count implementation? Select all that apply.

options.text: Only one input where every value appears twice.
One value appears many times while several others appear once.

feedback.reason: Frequency logic should be tested at minimal key count, maximal key count, and uneven multiplicity.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “All values are the same.”, “All values are distinct.”, “One value appears many times while several others appear once.”. These shapes expose incorrect initialization, key creation, and repeated increment behavior.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: Frequency logic should be tested at minimal key count, maximal key count, and uneven multiplicity.

items: Only one input where every value appears twice. — One symmetric case does not test extremes or skewed distributions.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.only_one_balanced_case: One symmetric case does not test extremes or skewed distributions.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.all_same: It verifies repeated updates to one key and the minimum distinct-key count.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.all_distinct: It verifies creation of one count entry per occurrence and the maximum distinct-key count.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.one_dominant_value: It checks that large and small counts coexist correctly.

items.prompt: An adjacent scan examines every pair in an array of length n. Select the number of pair checks and auxiliary-space complexity.
constraints: The algorithm uses only a constant number of local variables.

feedback.reason: Sequence length determines the number of adjacent boundaries, including the zero-pair edge cases.

blocks.text: Lengths 0 and 1 produce zero checks. For n >= 2, each boundary between neighboring elements is examined once, yielding n - 1 checks.

blocks.title: Complexity rule
blocks.text: Sequence length determines the number of adjacent boundaries, including the zero-pair edge cases.

items: pair checks: max(0, n - 1)
auxiliary space: O(1)
0 checks is correct only for n = 0 or n = 1, not for every possible input length.
n checks counts one nonexistent boundary after the final element.
n² checks would require comparing many non-adjacent pairs; this scan examines only neighboring boundaries.
O(n) or O(n²) auxiliary space would require growing state, but the stated algorithm keeps only fixed local variables.

items.prompt: A developer sorts an input before checking whether the original sequence alternates between two values. What is the main defect?

options.text: Sorting is unable to process sequences containing exactly two values.
Sorting is invalid because it always uses constant space.
Sorting destroys the original positional shape that defines alternation.

feedback.reason: Alternation is defined by the original order of neighboring positions.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “Sorting destroys the original positional shape that defines alternation.”. Sorting groups equal values and can turn an alternating sequence into runs. The multiset remains similar, but the shape relevant to the question is lost.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: Alternation is defined by the original order of neighboring positions.

items: Sorting automatically removes repeated values. — Sorting rearranges occurrences but does not delete them.
Sorting is unable to process sequences containing exactly two values. — Sorting can process such inputs; it simply violates the positional contract.
Sorting is invalid because it always uses constant space. — The premise is false because sorting algorithms have different space costs, and space usage does not address loss of original order.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sorting_removes_duplicates: Sorting rearranges occurrences but does not delete them.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sorting_cannot_handle_two_values: Sorting can process such inputs; it simply violates the positional contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sorting_constant_space: The premise is false because sorting algorithms have different space costs, and space usage does not address loss of original order.

items.prompt: A function removes only consecutive duplicates. What should it return for [1, 2, 1]?

feedback.reason: The repeated 1 values are separated, so the sequence contains no consecutive duplicate run.

blocks.text: The correct choice is “[1, 2, 1]”. The input shape matters: global repetition does not imply adjacent repetition. Every original occurrence remains under the consecutive-only contract.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: The repeated 1 values are separated, so the sequence contains no consecutive duplicate run.

items: [1, 2] — This applies global deduplication rather than consecutive-run collapse.
[1] — This removes distinct and non-consecutive values without justification.
[1, 2], because sorting is implied — Sorting is not implied and would change the original sequence shape.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.global_unique: This applies global deduplication rather than consecutive-run collapse.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_only: This removes distinct and non-consecutive values without justification.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sorted_unique: Sorting is not implied and would change the original sequence shape.
